newsitem.title: USA: Advertisers, states fight over FDA tobacco rules.
newsitem.headline: Advertisers, states fight over FDA tobacco rules.

text.p: Federal rules for stricter limits on cigarette advertising have been challenged by the tobacco industry, advertising groups and convenience stores. More than half the states have expressed support for the rules, proposed last year to curb smoking among children.
The Food and Drug Administration's proposed new regulations would:
-- Ban vending machines except in some nightclubs and other places where people under 18 cannot enter.
-- Ban billboards within 1,000 feet of schools and playgrounds.
-- Limit other billboard and in-store advertising to black-and-white text only, unless the ad was in a place that excluded people under 18.
-- Limit print ads likely to be seen by youngsters to black-and-white text only.
-- Ban brand-name sponsorship of sporting or other events. Corporate name sponsorship would be permitted.
-- Ban cigarette names on hats, T-shirts, gym bags and other products.
